npcRoster.name: Cogsworth Brasswell
npcRoster.publicDescription: Cogsworth Brasswell is a polished, fussy, heartbreakingly loyal Warforged steward built for domestic care, household order, childcare, gardening, and ceremonial hospitality. As one of Setrimir’s awakened constructs, he clings to routine because routine is how he proves love: every swept hall, mended kettle, trimmed hedge, and warmed hearth becomes an act of devotion rather than mere programming. Beneath his bright manners and brass-button propriety is a lonely, anxious soul terrified that the people he cares for may never come home, so he pretends the household can still be saved if he simply keeps everything ready. In Bronzewake, he serves with the Freeblade Veil, restoring abandoned homes and ruined family estates for refugees, heirs, debtors, and displaced households. His work at the Old Household Manse makes him part steward, part caretaker, part grief counselor, and part walking emergency protocol for families trying to rebuild in Virelport’s capital.

npcRoster.publicDescription: Pammora Loom is a calm, unnerving Golynn oracle who speaks in probability threads instead of prophecy, mapping danger through repeated names, train delays, ration shortages, and ichor purchase patterns. The Freeblade Veil relies on them to predict raids before agents have evidence, though their warnings often sound absurd until the ambush happens exactly where they said it would. Pammora is gentle with frightened people and merciless with bad data.

npcRoster.publicDescription: Ser Dain Calvorr is a disciplined Warforged skyship paladin whose whole identity was built around order, honorable command, and the belief that dangerous relics belong under armed custody. The Crucible Wardens still see him as a weapon and symbol, but he is slowly becoming someone who can decide whether loyalty means obedience, protection, or refusal.

npcRoster.name: Faradai Coil
npcRoster.publicDescription: Faradai Coil is a Gnome archivist engineer who keeps the Stormgullet Workshop running with solder burns, sleepless notes, and the brittle patience of someone surrounded by people who think ideals repair machinery. He maintains old refuge systems, power relays, memory devices, and transit safeguards for the Choral Synod, often acting as the practical counterweight to philosophers and fugitives. Faradai is loyal, irritable, and afraid that one failed mechanism will expose every protected person he ever promised to keep hidden.

npcRoster.name: Keleo Briarvast
npcRoster.publicDescription:
Keleo Briarvast is calm, elegant, openly dangerous, and almost insultingly polite about how many ways she knows to end a conversation permanently. As a Firbolg, she carries Anubaldir’s quiet inheritance of hidden strength, endurance, and protective stewardship, but in Stormgullet that guardian instinct has hardened into territorial paranoia: her shop, her clients, and her secrets are all things she protects with lethal precision.
At the Velvet Armory, Keleo sells black-market blades, firearms, thundercoil weapons, warded ammunition, explosives, and discreet “problem-solving packages” to anyone with enough coin and enough nerve. Her work with the Brass Concordat makes her less a simple merchant and more a contingency planner for Virelport’s underworld, keeping private kill-ledgers on rivals, militia captains, informants, and anyone foolish enough to threaten her business while the province’s street-level corruption and transit politics keep everyone looking elsewhere.

npcRoster.name: Veyr of Seventeen Names
npcRoster.publicDescription:
Veyr of Seventeen Names is charming, evasive, and almost compulsively dishonest about their own history, but their lies are usually armor wrapped around guilt rather than simple cruelty. As a Changeling shaped by Thalunesh’s influence over shapeshifters, wanderers, tricks, and misdirection, they treat identity like a tool, a weapon, and a wound all at once.
For the Freeblade Veil, Veyr works as a false-name spy out of the Freeblade Safehouse, watching docks, taverns, transit ledgers, shrine records, and faction offices for signs that someone vulnerable is about to be exposed. In Veilstrand, where Virelport’s corruption, transit politics, missing workers, and sealed divine mechanisms already make truth dangerous, Veyr specializes in moving people before the law realizes which name to arrest.

Changeling reads through the Lorwyn Changeling entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Lorwyn changelings are fey-adapted shapeshifters tied to idyllic, magical realms. They often blend seamlessly into multiple cultures and identities.
